The Play dev-link walkthrough (note 3 months in the diary, start a new diagnosis, conclude, see 'do diário, medido' on the result) was not run: it needs the Play desktop runtime and the frontend screens. The same path is covered at API level (diagnosisRoutes.test.ts: 3 months -> draft -> complete -> calculator.diarySource and unitEconomics.origin measured).

server/validation/backupSchemas.ts restores a diagnosis' calculator through diagnosisPatchSchema.shape.calculator (strict). Keeping that schema strict would have made any backup containing a diagnosis with diary marks fail to restore (422 backup_invalid). So diagnosisPatchSchema now carries the stored calculator shape (spendTotalCents, diarySource, diarySuggestion) and refuses the two diary keys with a superRefine on the PATCH (400, field calculator.diarySource / calculator.diarySuggestion). Result: a client can never send marks, and a backup keeps and restores them (round trip covered by a test in diagnosisRoutes.test.ts). backupSchemas.ts and backupService.ts were not touched.

messages.text: IF-007 as built. src/api/diagnosesApi.ts: applyDiarySuggestion(id) -> POST /api/diagnoses/:id/diary-suggestion, no body, answers the whole Diagnosis (replace local state with it). 409 no_diary_suggestion when the draft has no suggestion (3+ months or no month), 409 diagnosis_not_draft once completed, 404 diagnosis_not_found. Diagnosis.calculator now carries spendTotalCents (single total, spendParts {} then), diarySource {spend?, newCustomers?} ({origin measured|estimated, fromMonth, toMonth, monthCount}) and diarySuggestion (null/absent when none). The server decides the marks: updateDiagnosis() strips diarySource/diarySuggestion from patch.calculator before sending (the PATCH refuses them with 400), and a number sent again with the same value keeps its mark, so autosaving the whole block is safe; typing a different value removes only that field's mark. Use shared/domain/diaryPrefill.ts helpers for the screens: formatDiaryMark(source) -> 'do diário: ago/2026 a out/2026' | 'do diário: 2 meses, estimado'; isDiarySuggestionOffered(calculator) for 'Usar o diário'; getCostDiaryOrigin(calculator) + formatCostDiaryOrigin(origin) -> 'do diário, medido' | 'do diário, estimado' (null means typed, show nothing extra). A new CalculatorPatch type (calculator without the two diary keys) is exported next to DiagnosisPatch.

diagnosisPatchSchema (server/validation/diagnosisSchemas.ts) now has the stored calculator shape (spendTotalCents, diarySource, diarySuggestion) and a superRefine that refuses the two diary keys in a request. This is on purpose: server/validation/backupSchemas.ts builds the restore schema from diagnosisPatchSchema.shape.calculator, so a backup of a diagnosis with diary marks restores. If someone later wants a request-only calculator schema, build it separately instead of tightening .shape.calculator, or backups with marks will stop restoring. readStoredCalculator now returns StoredCalculator (a superset of CalculatorPatch); historyService, homeService, reportService and backupService already read through it, so recalculation of an older diagnosis (RULE-ra-02) keeps the diary 'estimated' origin.

Reports. (1) Diagnosis PDF: reportModel ReportInput/DiagnosisDocumentInput gain costDiaryOrigin ('measured'|'estimated'|null); reportService fills it from the stored calculator (getCostDiaryOrigin) even without includeAnswers, and only the origin travels, never a typed value (BR-ra-08 test added). 'Seus números' then reads 'R$ X (do diário, medido|estimado)'; the cost keeps its first-version wording when it was typed or could not be calculated. With includeAnswers, the answers appendix marks the spend and new-customers rows that still carry a diary mark and now prints a diary single total (it used to print R$ 0,00 for total-only spend). (2) Evolution PDF: server/report/evolutionDocument.ts exports buildPeriodDiary(entries, from, to); reportService passes period.diary from the company's diary: usable months from the month of the earlier diagnosis through the month of the later one, both included, oldest first, cost per customer per month ('não calculado' with 0 new customers). The page 'O que foi feito no período' now appears with only diary months too, and keeps showing the 6 most recent months of the period.
